name: Companion Tent
summary: A small canvas tent stitched together for a single companion to nap in; the first and easiest companion house.
wit: Room for one, snacks for two.
trivia: Early tents were made from animal hides stretched over wooden poles.
artBrief: Small triangular tent with open flap, sandy canvas, brown poles, dark entrance; centred, bold outline.

name: Companion Hut
summary: A cosy wooden hut with a low doorway that shelters two companions from wind and rain.
trivia: Huts are among the oldest kinds of shelter people have built, found on every inhabited continent.
artBrief: Round log hut with cone roof and dark doorway, warm brown, tan roof, green base; front view.

name: Companion Cabin
summary: A sturdy log cabin with a proper front door, big enough for three companions to live together.
trivia: Log cabins became common in North America after settlers from Scandinavia and Finland brought the building style in the 1600s.
artBrief: Log cabin with stacked logs, red door, small window; brown, red, cream; slight 3/4 view.

name: Companion Cottage
summary: A charming cottage with a smoking chimney and a warm fireplace inside, home for four companions.
wit: Smoke signals mean dinner is ready.
trivia: Many traditional cottages were built around a central hearth, with the chimney added later to carry smoke out.
artBrief: White-walled cottage, red tiled roof, chimney with grey puff, yellow lit window; front view.

name: Companion Villa
summary: A roomy two-storey villa with a grand staircase where six companions each get space to roam.
trivia: Roman villas were often country houses built around a courtyard and could include baths and gardens.
artBrief: Two-storey cream villa, terracotta roof, arched windows, small balcony; cream, orange, teal.

name: Companion Castle
summary: A grand little castle with towers and a winched gate, the largest companion house, sheltering eight companions.
trivia: Medieval castles often took a decade or more to build.
artBrief: Small castle with two round towers, flag, arched gate; grey stone, blue roofs, red flag; front view.

name: Fabric
summary: A soft sheet of woven cloth fresh off the loom, ready to be cut and sewn into home goods.
trivia: Woven fabric is made by interlacing two sets of threads called the warp and the weft.
artBrief: Folded stack of cloth with a visible weave texture; soft blue, lighter blue edge, white stitch.

name: Rope
summary: Strong twisted cord made by winding many strands of yarn together, used for tying and hanging.
wit: Learning the ropes, one twist at a time.
trivia: Traditional ropewalks used hand cranks to twist long strands of fibre into rope.
artBrief: Coiled rope loop with twisted texture; tan and brown, dark outline; centred.

name: Saw
summary: A toothed hand saw that cuts logs and planks to size on the workbench.
wit: It has seen things. Mostly wood.
trivia: Saws with teeth date back to ancient Egypt, where copper saws were used to cut wood.
artBrief: Hand saw with wooden handle and toothed silver blade, diagonal; silver, brown, dark grey.

name: Nail
summary: A small pointed pin hammered into wood to fasten boards and furniture together.
trivia: Before machines, nails were made one at a time by blacksmiths and were valuable enough to be reused.
artBrief: Single nail, diagonal, round flat head; steel grey with light highlight; bold outline.

name: Wooden Peg
summary: A short rounded wooden pin used to join beams, hold shelves and hang things on walls.
wit: A tiny stick with a big job.
trivia: Old timber-frame houses were often held together with wooden pegs instead of metal nails.
artBrief: Two short wooden dowel pegs crossed; light tan wood with darker end grain.

name: Wooden Beam
summary: A long squared timber cut from a log, the backbone of floors, roofs and frames.
trivia: Some oak beams in old buildings are over 600 years old and still holding up roofs.
artBrief: Long rectangular timber beam at an angle, wood grain lines; brown, dark brown, tan.

name: Floorboards
summary: Rows of planks laid side by side to make a smooth wooden floor inside a house.
wit: Creaks included at no extra cost.
trivia: Wide floorboards in old houses usually came from very large old-growth trees.
artBrief: Square of parallel wooden boards in perspective; honey, brown, dark seams.

name: Wood Shavings
summary: Thin curly ribbons of wood peeled off planks while smoothing them at the bench.
trivia: Fine wood shavings, called wood wool or excelsior, were once a common stuffing and packing material.
artBrief: Pile of curly pale wood ribbons; cream, tan, light brown curls.

name: Wooden Bucket
summary: A round bucket made from planks held tight by hoops, for carrying water, paint or glue.
trivia: Coopers build buckets and barrels from curved staves held together by hoops, without any glue.
artBrief: Wooden bucket with two dark hoops and rope handle; brown staves, grey hoops; front view.

name: Glue
summary: A thick sticky paste for bonding wood, cloth and paper together in the workshop.
trivia: People have made glues for thousands of years; birch-bark tar used as glue is over 200,000 years old.
artBrief: Small pot of white glue with drip on side and brush stick; white, cream, brown pot.

name: Paint
summary: A bucket of bright coloured paint for walls, doors and furniture.
trivia: Early paints were made by mixing ground minerals such as ochre with water, fat or egg.
artBrief: Bucket of paint with a colourful drip over the rim; red, yellow, blue drips, grey bucket.

name: Varnish
summary: A clear glossy coating brushed onto wood to protect it and make the grain shine.
wit: Shiny on the outside, wood on the inside.
trivia: Many traditional varnishes were made from tree resins dissolved in oil.
artBrief: Small jar of amber liquid with a gleam and brush; amber, gold, brown lid.

name: Wallpaper
summary: A roll of patterned decorative sheets glued onto walls to brighten up a room.
trivia: Wallpaper became popular in Europe in the 1500s as a cheaper alternative to tapestries.
artBrief: Partly unrolled wallpaper roll with flower pattern; pink, cream, green.

name: Door
summary: A hinged wooden door that fits into an archway and opens the way into any home.
wit: The best way to make an entrance.
trivia: Some of the oldest known doors, found in Switzerland, are around 5,000 years old.
artBrief: Arched wooden door with round knob and plank lines; brown, darker brown, gold knob.

name: Window Frame
summary: A wooden frame with crossbars that holds a window in a wall and lets daylight in.
trivia: The crossbars dividing window panes are called muntins.
artBrief: Square wooden window frame with cross of bars, light blue panes; white frame, light blue.

name: Curtain
summary: Soft fabric drapes hung across a window frame to keep out bright light and add colour.
trivia: Theatre curtains inspired the phrase "curtain call", the moment performers return to bow.
artBrief: Two red drapes tied back from a window frame; red, dark red folds, white frame.

name: Roof
summary: A sloped covering of beams and boards that keeps rain, snow and sun off a house.
wit: Top of the house, top of the class.
trivia: A steep roof sheds snow and rain faster, which is why many houses in snowy places have tall pointed roofs.
artBrief: Triangular roof with rafters visible underneath; red, brown, dark outline.

name: Ladder
summary: Two wooden rails joined by pegged rungs, used to climb up to lofts, shelves and rooftops.
wit: Step by step, rung by rung.
trivia: Ladders are shown in Spanish cave paintings that are about 10,000 years old.
artBrief: Upright wooden ladder with five rungs; light brown rails, darker rungs.

name: Staircase
summary: A flight of wooden steps that joins one floor of a house to the next.
wit: Taking things to the next level.
trivia: The vertical part of a stair step is called the riser, and the part you step on is the tread.
artBrief: Side view of a zigzag wooden staircase with handrail; brown, tan, dark rail.

name: Shelf
summary: A flat board resting on pegs against the wall, ready to hold books, pots and treasures.
trivia: Adjustable bookshelves often use small pegs called shelf pins to hold each board.
artBrief: Single wall shelf with two pegs and a tiny pot on top; brown, tan, green pot.

name: Wooden Crate
summary: A slatted box nailed together from planks, handy for storing and carrying things.
trivia: Wooden crates were the main shipping containers before cardboard boxes became common in the 1900s.
artBrief: Slatted wooden crate in 3/4 view with nail dots; light brown, dark slats.

name: Drawer
summary: A sliding wooden box with a knob, the key part of dressers, desks and cabinets.
trivia: Chests of drawers became popular in the 1600s, replacing simple lidded chests.
artBrief: Single wooden drawer pulled out slightly with round knob; brown, gold knob.

name: Pillow Stuffing
summary: A fluffy bundle of soft filling used to plump up pillows, cushions and mattresses.
trivia: Before modern fibres, pillows were stuffed with feathers, straw, wool or even wood wool.
artBrief: Puffy cloud-like bundle of white fluff with a few fibre wisps; white, light grey, pale blue.

name: Pillow
summary: A soft stuffed fabric pillow that makes beds and naps much more comfortable.
trivia: Ancient Mesopotamians used pillows made of stone, mainly to keep their heads off the ground.
artBrief: Plump rectangular white pillow with corner puffs; white, light blue shade.

name: Cushion
summary: A plump square cushion placed on the floor where a companion can sit and relax.
trivia: Floor cushions are a traditional form of seating in many homes around the world, including Japan and the Middle East.
artBrief: Square plump cushion with centre button tuft; purple, lighter purple, gold button.

name: Quilt
summary: A warm quilt of patchwork squares sewn over a soft layer of stuffing.
wit: Patch by patch, warmth by warmth.
trivia: A quilt has three layers: a top, a soft middle called batting, and a backing.
artBrief: Square patchwork quilt with coloured squares and stitch lines; red, yellow, blue, cream.

name: Mattress
summary: A thick padded mattress that turns any bed frame into a proper place to sleep.
wit: Like a pillow, but for everything.
trivia: Early mattresses were stuffed with straw, wool or feathers and laid on the floor or on rope frames.
artBrief: Thick rectangular mattress in 3/4 view with tufts; white, pale blue stripes.

name: Bed Frame
summary: A sturdy wooden frame with legs and a headboard, waiting for a mattress on top.
trivia: The phrase "sleep tight" is often linked to old beds whose rope supports had to be pulled tight.
artBrief: Empty wooden bed frame with headboard in side view; brown, dark brown.

name: Rug
summary: A soft woven rug spread across the floorboards to make a room warm and colourful.
trivia: The Pazyryk carpet, found in a frozen Siberian tomb, is about 2,400 years old.
artBrief: Rectangular rug with border pattern and tassels, top view; red, gold, navy.

name: Doormat
summary: A rough little mat placed by the door so companions can wipe their paws before coming in.
trivia: Coir doormats are made from the tough fibres of coconut husks.
artBrief: Small rectangular brown mat with a little paw print; tan, brown, dark paw.

name: Lamp Shade
summary: A round fabric shade stretched over a ring frame that softens the glow of a lamp.
trivia: Lamp shades became widespread with oil and then electric lamps, to soften harsh glare.
artBrief: Drum-shaped fabric lamp shade, slightly tapered; cream, warm yellow glow, dark rim.

name: Fence
summary: A short picket fence of planks on beams that borders a companion yard.
trivia: Picket fences take their name from the pointed stakes, or pickets, used in old military defences.
artBrief: Three white pickets with pointed tops on two rails; white, light grey, green grass strip.

name: Toolbox
summary: A handy wooden box with a carry handle that keeps every building tool in one place.
wit: A place for every tool, and every tool in its place.
trivia: Carpenters traditionally built their own tool chests as a showcase of their skill.
artBrief: Open wooden toolbox with handle, tool handles poking out; brown, red handle, silver.

name: Basket
summary: A woven basket with a handle for carrying snacks, yarn and small home treasures.
trivia: Basket weaving is one of the oldest crafts, with remains dating back over 10,000 years.
artBrief: Woven basket with arched handle and criss-cross texture; tan, golden brown.

name: Kindling
summary: A small bundle of dry twigs and shavings used to start a fire in a hearth.
trivia: Kindling sits between tinder and logs: it catches fire from tinder and then lights the bigger wood.
artBrief: Bundle of small sticks tied with string over curly shavings; tan, brown, cream.

name: Fireplace
summary: A warm arched fireplace with crackling kindling where companions gather to relax.
trivia: Before central heating, the fireplace was often the only heat source and cooking spot in a home.
artBrief: Brick fireplace arch with orange flames on logs; red-brown, orange, yellow, dark opening.

name: Chimney
summary: A tall stack that rises through the roof and carries smoke up and away from the fireplace.
wit: Up, up and away, says the smoke.
trivia: Chimneys became common in European homes around the 1100s and 1200s.
artBrief: Brick chimney on a roof slope with grey smoke puff; red brick, grey, brown roof.

name: Castle Gate
summary: A heavy arched gate raised and lowered by a crank, the grand entrance of any castle.
wit: Crank it up, let them in.
trivia: The sliding grille gate of many castles is called a portcullis, raised by winches and chains.
artBrief: Arched gate with vertical bars half raised and side crank wheel; grey, brown, dark opening.

name: Blanket
summary: A thick soft blanket woven from yarn and fabric to keep companions warm at night.
trivia: The word blanket may come from blanc, French for white, the colour of undyed wool cloth.
artBrief: Folded blanket with fringed edge and stripe; teal, cream stripe, soft shadow.

name: Diamond
summary: A brilliant, ultra-hard gemstone of pure carbon, squeezed into shape deep underground over ages.
trivia: Diamond is the hardest natural material on Earth.
artBrief: Faceted cut diamond, front view, pale cyan, white highlight, dark outline.

name: Bat
summary: A small furry flying mammal that sleeps upside down in caves and hunts insects at night.
trivia: Bats are the only mammals capable of true powered flight.
artBrief: Dark purple bat with spread wings, small fangs, centered, lilac belly.

name: Jungle
summary: A dense, tangled tropical forest packed with hanging vines, huge leaves and noisy wildlife.
trivia: Jungles can hold more than half of all land species in a tiny area.
artBrief: Thick green canopy with hanging vines, two shades of green and brown trunks.

name: Bear
summary: A big, strong furry mammal of the woods that loves fish, berries and especially honey.
trivia: Bears can smell food from several kilometres away.
artBrief: Brown bear sitting, holding a small yellow honey pot, round shapes.

name: Camel
summary: A long-legged desert animal with a hump that can walk for days between oases without drinking.
wit: Packs its lunch in its back.
trivia: A camel hump stores fat, not water.
artBrief: Tan one-hump camel in side view, sandy yellow ground line.

name: Snowman
summary: A friendly figure built from stacked snowballs, with a carrot nose and twig arms.
trivia: The tallest snowman ever built was over 37 metres tall.
artBrief: Three white snowballs stacked, orange carrot nose, red scarf, light blue outline.

name: Steel
summary: A strong, tough alloy of iron and a little carbon, used for bridges, tools and machines.
trivia: Ancient smiths made steel by heating iron with charcoal.
artBrief: Grey steel I-beam in perspective, blue-grey shading, white shine.

name: Axe
summary: A woodcutting tool with a heavy steel head on a wooden handle, used to chop logs and firewood.
trivia: Stone axes are among the oldest tools humans ever made.
artBrief: Axe with brown wooden handle and grey steel head, diagonal.

name: Beach
summary: A sunny strip of soft sand where the sea meets the land, full of shells and waves.
wit: Sand in places you forgot existed.
trivia: Some beaches have pink or black sand from coral or volcanic rock.
artBrief: Yellow sand strip, blue wave edge, small orange sun in corner.

name: Candle
summary: A stick of wax with a wick that burns slowly to give a small, steady flame of light.
wit: A tiny campfire with good manners.
trivia: Early candles were made from beeswax or animal fat.
artBrief: Cream wax candle with orange flame and yellow core, dripping wax.

name: Grass
summary: Thin green blades that cover fields, lawns and meadows, feeding many grazing animals.
trivia: Grasslands cover about a quarter of Earth's land.
artBrief: Tuft of bright green grass blades on a brown soil strip.

name: Wheat
summary: A tall golden cereal grass whose grains are ground into flour for bread and pasta.
trivia: Wheat was one of the first crops farmed, over 10,000 years ago.
artBrief: Three golden wheat stalks with grain heads, crossed, warm yellow.

name: Chicken
summary: A farm bird that pecks at grain, clucks around the yard and lays eggs.
trivia: There are more chickens on Earth than any other bird.
artBrief: White hen with red comb, orange beak and feet, side view.

name: Earthquake
summary: A sudden shaking of the ground caused by moving rock deep inside the Earth.
wit: The ground having a bad day.
trivia: Thousands of small earthquakes happen every day around the world.
artBrief: Brown ground split by a zigzag crack, small shake lines on both sides.

name: Light Bulb
summary: A glass bulb with a glowing filament or LED that turns electricity into light.
trivia: Early bulbs used carbonised bamboo filaments.
artBrief: Classic yellow-glowing bulb with grey screw base, light rays.

name: Seagull
summary: A noisy white-and-grey seabird that glides over coasts and steals snacks from beachgoers.
trivia: Gulls can drink salt water and expel the salt through glands.
artBrief: White gull with grey wings, yellow beak, gliding, light blue background dot.

name: Palm Tree
summary: A tall tropical tree with a bare trunk and a crown of big fan or feather leaves.
trivia: Coconuts can float across oceans to start new palms.
artBrief: Curved brown trunk, green fronds, two brown coconuts.

name: Wolf
summary: A wild grey canine that lives and hunts in packs and famously howls at night.
wit: Sings to the moon, never off-key.
trivia: Wolves are the wild ancestors of pet dogs.
artBrief: Grey wolf sitting, head up howling, pale yellow moon behind.

name: Dog
summary: A loyal, playful companion animal descended from wolves and tamed by people long ago.
trivia: Dogs were the first animals humans domesticated.
artBrief: Friendly brown dog sitting, tongue out, floppy ears.

name: Cat
summary: A small, curious furry pet with whiskers that purrs, naps in the sun and chases toys.
trivia: Cats spend about two thirds of their lives sleeping.
artBrief: Orange cat sitting, tail curled, green eyes, front view.

name: Cow
summary: A gentle farm animal that grazes on grass all day and gives milk.
trivia: Cows have one stomach with four compartments.
artBrief: Black-and-white cow head, pink nose, small horns.

name: Sheep
summary: A fluffy farm animal covered in soft wool that grazes in flocks.
wit: A cloud that learned to walk.
trivia: A sheep's wool never stops growing.
artBrief: Round white woolly sheep with black face and legs.

name: Snake
summary: A long, legless reptile that slithers through grass and marshes and flicks its tongue.
trivia: Snakes smell with their tongues.
artBrief: Green snake in an S curve, forked red tongue.

name: Lizard
summary: A small scaly reptile with four legs and a long tail that loves basking in the sun.
trivia: Some lizards can drop and regrow their tails.
artBrief: Green lizard top view, curled tail, yellow sun spot.

name: Crocodile
summary: A huge armoured reptile with powerful jaws that lurks in rivers waiting for prey.
wit: Smiles a lot. Do not smile back.
trivia: Crocodiles have barely changed since the age of dinosaurs.
artBrief: Dark green crocodile side view, open toothy jaws, blue water line.

name: Whale
summary: A gigantic ocean mammal that breathes air through a blowhole and sings deep songs.
trivia: The blue whale is the largest animal that has ever lived.
artBrief: Big blue whale with water spout, pale belly, side view.

name: Savanna
summary: A warm, wide grassland with scattered trees, home to lions, zebras and giraffes.
wit: Grass as far as the eye can roam.
trivia: Savannas cover nearly half of Africa.
artBrief: Yellow grass plain, flat-topped acacia tree, orange sky band.

name: Lion
summary: A big wild cat with a golden coat; males wear a shaggy mane and roar across the savanna.
wit: King of the jungle, lives on the savanna.
trivia: A lion's roar can be heard 8 km away.
artBrief: Lion head front view, golden face, big brown mane.

name: Rust
summary: The flaky reddish-brown coating that forms when iron is left in water and air.
trivia: Rust is iron oxide, the same compound that makes Mars red.
artBrief: Grey metal plate with orange-brown rust patches.

name: Atoll
summary: A ring-shaped coral reef or island circling a calm blue lagoon in the open ocean.
trivia: Atolls often form on top of sunken volcanoes.
artBrief: Top view green-yellow ring island, turquoise lagoon, dark blue sea.

name: Worm
summary: A soft, wriggly creature that tunnels through mud and soil and keeps it healthy.
trivia: Earthworms breathe through their skin.
artBrief: Pink wiggly worm on brown soil band.

name: Snowflake
summary: A tiny six-pointed ice crystal that drifts down from winter clouds.
trivia: Nearly every snowflake has six sides.
artBrief: Six-point white snowflake on light blue circle.

name: Soap
summary: A bar made from oils and ash-lye that foams with water and washes dirt away.
trivia: Ancient Babylonians made soap from fats and ash.
artBrief: Pink soap bar with three white bubbles.

name: Milkshake
summary: A thick, cold drink of milk blended with ice cream, often topped with cream.
trivia: Electric blenders made milkshakes popular in the 1920s.
artBrief: Tall glass with pink shake, whipped cream, red cherry, striped straw.

name: Mountain Goat
summary: A sure-footed white goat that climbs steep rocky cliffs with ease.
trivia: Mountain goats can jump nearly 4 metres in one bound.
artBrief: White goat with small black horns on a grey rock ledge.

name: French Fries
summary: Crispy golden sticks of fried potato, sprinkled with salt.
trivia: Belgium and France both claim to have invented fries.
artBrief: Red paper cone overflowing with golden fries.

name: Grape
summary: Small sweet round fruits that grow in bunches on climbing vines.
trivia: Raisins are just dried grapes.
artBrief: Purple grape bunch with a green leaf.

name: Mermaid
summary: A legendary sea person with a human upper body and a shimmering fish tail.
wit: Half swimmer, half fish, all legend.
trivia: Mermaid legends appear in cultures all over the world.
artBrief: Mermaid side view, teal tail, red hair, simple shapes.

name: Unicorn
summary: A magical white horse with a single spiral horn, said to be pure and very rare.
trivia: The unicorn is the national animal of Scotland.
artBrief: White horse head with golden spiral horn, pink mane.

name: Fairy
summary: A tiny winged spirit of folklore who lives in hidden mounds and woods and grants small magic.
trivia: In Irish lore, fairies live in hills called sidhe.
artBrief: Tiny fairy with clear blue wings, green dress, sparkle trail.

name: Thunderbird
summary: A giant legendary bird whose wing beats make thunder and whose eyes flash lightning.
wit: Its flapping is in the forecast.
trivia: The Thunderbird is a powerful spirit in many Indigenous North American traditions.
artBrief: Big bird with spread wings, yellow lightning zigzags, dark blue.

name: Yeti
summary: A shaggy white ape-like creature said to roam the snowy Himalayan mountains.
trivia: Yeti stories come from Himalayan folklore; many "Yeti" samples proved to be bears.
artBrief: White furry creature with blue face, arms raised, snowy ground.

name: Karaoke
summary: Singing along to music while the lyrics scroll on a screen, just for fun.
trivia: The word karaoke is Japanese for "empty orchestra".
artBrief: Microphone in front of a screen with lyric bars, purple and pink.

name: Screenplay
summary: The written script of a film, with scenes, dialogue and directions for the actors.
trivia: A screenplay page runs about one minute of screen time.
artBrief: Stack of white script pages with brass fasteners and a film clapper icon.

name: Hourglass
summary: A two-bulb glass timer in which sand trickles from the top to the bottom.
trivia: Hourglasses were used on ships to measure speed.
artBrief: Hourglass with wooden caps, yellow sand, light blue glass.

name: Bed
summary: A sturdy wooden bed frame topped with a soft mattress, where a companion sleeps and recovers health overnight.
wit: Five more minutes. Then five more.
trivia: Ancient Egyptian beds often sloped slightly and had a footboard so sleepers would not slide off.
artBrief: Single bed side view, brown frame, white mattress, blue blanket; bold outline, flat colours.

name: Pet Bed
summary: A round woven basket lined with a plump cushion, sized perfectly for a small companion to curl up in.
trivia: Many dogs and cats circle before lying down, an instinct thought to come from flattening grass in the wild.
artBrief: Round wicker basket with red cushion, tan weave, top 3/4 view; centred, thick outline.

name: Bunk Bed
summary: Two beds stacked one above the other with a ladder up the side, so two companions can share a small room.
trivia: Bunk beds have long been used on ships, in barracks and at camps where space is limited.
artBrief: Two stacked beds with side ladder, brown wood, blue and red blankets; front view.

name: Canopy Bed
summary: A grand bed with four tall posts and flowing curtains draped overhead, making a cosy private nest for sleeping.
trivia: Bed curtains once helped keep sleepers warm in cold, draughty castles and manor houses.
artBrief: Four-poster bed with pink drapes tied at posts, brown wood, white sheets; front 3/4 view.

name: Stool
summary: A simple round wooden seat on three or four pegged legs, with no back and no arms, light enough to carry anywhere.
trivia: A three-legged stool never wobbles, because three points always rest steadily on any surface.
artBrief: Round-top three-legged stool, light brown, darker leg shading; side view, bold outline.

name: Chair
summary: A wooden seat with four legs and an upright backrest, the everyday chair every room eventually needs.
wit: A stool that learned to lean back.
trivia: For centuries chairs were rare luxuries, and most ordinary people sat on benches or stools.
artBrief: Plain wooden chair with slatted back, mid brown, side 3/4 view; thick outline.

name: Armchair
summary: A deep padded chair with soft armrests on both sides, perfect for sinking into after a long day.
wit: Designed for one, defended by all.
trivia: Upholstered armchairs became popular in the 1700s as padding and springs improved.
artBrief: Chunky green armchair with rounded arms and cushion, front 3/4 view; green, dark green, brown feet.

name: Sofa
summary: A long padded couch with room for several companions to sit, sprawl or doze side by side.
wit: Where lost snacks go to live.
trivia: The word sofa comes from an Arabic word for a raised platform covered with carpets and cushions.
artBrief: Three-seat sofa, orange-red upholstery, two cushions, short brown legs; front view.

name: Rocking Chair
summary: A wooden chair set on two curved rockers so it sways gently back and forth when someone sits in it.
trivia: Rocking chairs became widely popular in North America in the 1700s.
artBrief: Wooden rocking chair with curved runners, warm brown, red seat pad; side view.

name: Footstool
summary: A low padded stool for resting tired feet, or for a tiny companion to use as a throne.
trivia: Footstools were once a sign of status, keeping important feet off cold stone floors.
artBrief: Low square padded footstool, purple top, gold trim, stubby brown legs; 3/4 view.

name: Bean Bag
summary: A big floppy fabric sack filled with stuffing that squashes into whatever shape the sitter needs.
trivia: Bean bag chairs first became a hit in the late 1960s.
artBrief: Slumped teardrop bean bag, bright blue with lighter highlight, seam line; front view.

name: Side Table
summary: A small square wooden table that sits beside a chair or sofa to hold a lamp, a book or a cup of cocoa.
trivia: Small occasional tables became popular in the 1700s as rooms filled with more movable furniture.
artBrief: Small square wooden table on four legs, warm brown top, darker legs; 3/4 view.

name: Coffee Table
summary: A low table placed in front of the sofa to hold cups, books and the occasional napping companion.
trivia: Low tables in front of sofas became fashionable in Western homes in the late 1800s.
artBrief: Low oval wooden table with short legs, honey brown, cup on top; front 3/4 view.

name: Wardrobe
summary: A tall wooden cabinet with doors and drawers for hanging clothes, scarves and companion costumes.
wit: Check the back for other worlds.
trivia: Before built-in closets were common, most clothes were kept in freestanding wardrobes and chests.
artBrief: Tall two-door wardrobe, dark brown, round gold knobs, drawer at base; front view.

name: Dresser
summary: A wide chest of stacked drawers for folding away clothes, socks and treasured trinkets.
wit: Every drawer has one lonely sock.
trivia: Chests of drawers grew out of simple lidded chests during the 1600s.
artBrief: Wide three-drawer dresser, light oak, round knobs, front view; tan, brown, gold.

name: Nightstand
summary: A small bedside table with a drawer, just right for a glass of water and a bedtime story.
trivia: Bedside cabinets were once used to hide chamber pots out of sight.
artBrief: Small square bedside table with one drawer, brown, small knob; front view.

name: Floor Lamp
summary: A tall standing lamp with a fabric shade on a wooden pole that bathes a corner in warm light.
wit: The tallest thing that never grows.
trivia: Fabric lampshades soften and spread light so it is gentler on the eyes.
artBrief: Tall lamp, cream cone shade glowing yellow, thin brown pole, round base; front view.

name: Writing Desk
summary: A study desk with a smooth top and small drawers for paper and pens, where great ideas get written down.
trivia: Some antique writing desks hid secret compartments for letters and valuables.
artBrief: Wooden desk with drawers on one side, paper on top, brown and cream; 3/4 view.

name: Desk Lamp
summary: A small adjustable lamp that shines a focused pool of light onto the desk for late-night reading.
trivia: The balanced-arm desk lamp, which holds any position, was invented in the 1930s.
artBrief: Angled desk lamp with bent arm, green shade, yellow light cone; side view.

name: Bookshelf
summary: A tall set of wooden shelves packed with books, maps and notes that spark new ideas.
trivia: Libraries in ancient times stored scrolls in pigeonhole shelves rather than upright books.
artBrief: Tall bookshelf with colourful book spines on three shelves, brown frame; front view.

name: Secret Bookcase
summary: A bookcase that swings open like a door when the right book is pulled, revealing a hidden study.
wit: Pull the red one. No, the other red one.
trivia: Hidden doors disguised as bookcases were built in some old houses to conceal passages and rooms.
artBrief: Bookshelf half-swung open revealing dark gap, one tilted red book; brown, red, black.

name: Library Ladder
summary: A rolling ladder that slides along a tall bookcase so companions can reach the highest shelves.
trivia: Rolling library ladders run on a rail fixed to the bookcase and have been used since the 1700s.
artBrief: Tall bookcase with leaning wooden ladder on rail, brown, multicolour spines; front view.

name: Reading Chair
summary: A deep armchair tucked beside a glowing floor lamp, the perfect spot to lose an afternoon in a book.
trivia: Good reading light comes from behind or beside the reader to avoid glare on the page.
artBrief: Armchair with tall lamp behind, open book on seat; green, cream, yellow glow.

name: Globe Stand
summary: A painted spinning sphere of the world mounted on a wooden stand, perfect for dreaming up journeys.
wit: Spin it, point, pack a bag.
trivia: The oldest surviving terrestrial globe, the Erdapfel, was made in Germany in 1492.
artBrief: Blue globe with green continents on tilted brass ring, brown wooden stand; front view.

name: Window Seat
summary: A cushioned bench built beneath a window, where companions watch the rain and daydream.
wit: Front row seat to the weather.
trivia: Window seats were common in Georgian and Victorian homes, often with storage hidden underneath.
artBrief: Window with blue sky panes, cushioned bench below with pillows; white, blue, pink.

name: Wall Clock
summary: A round clock hung on the wall from a nail, ticking away the hours of the companion day.
trivia: Clock hands move clockwise because they copy the way shadows move on a sundial in the Northern Hemisphere.
artBrief: Round clock face with black hands and numbers, wooden rim; front view; cream, brown, black.

name: Cuckoo Clock
summary: A carved clock shaped like a little house, with a tiny bird that pops out to call every hour.
wit: Cuckoo! It is exactly bird o'clock.
trivia: Cuckoo clocks are strongly associated with the Black Forest region of Germany since the 1700s.
artBrief: Small house-shaped clock with peaked roof, bird at little door, pinecone weights; brown, cream, red.

name: Grandfather Clock
summary: A tall wooden case clock with a swinging pendulum and a deep chime that fills the whole house.
wit: Old, tall and always on time.
trivia: The name comes from an 1876 song about a clock that stopped when its owner died.
artBrief: Tall narrow clock, round face on top, glass door with gold pendulum; dark brown, gold, cream.

name: Picture Frame
summary: A wooden frame holding a small painting or portrait to hang on the wall and brighten the room.
trivia: Elaborate gilded frames were often more expensive than the paintings they held.
artBrief: Gold rectangular frame around tiny green-hill painting; front view; gold, green, blue.

name: Tapestry
summary: A large woven wall hanging covered in colourful scenes that keeps a room warm and full of stories.
wit: A rug that wanted to see the view.
trivia: Woven wall hangings helped insulate cold stone walls in medieval castles.
artBrief: Hanging cloth with rod on top, red border, small tree scene; red, gold, green.

name: Toy Chest
summary: A painted wooden chest with a hinged lid, overflowing with balls, blocks and plush toys.
trivia: Safe modern toy chests use lid supports so the lid cannot slam shut on small fingers.
artBrief: Painted chest, lid open, ball and block peeking out; blue chest, yellow stars, red ball.

name: Dollhouse
summary: A miniature house with tiny rooms and furniture, where companions stage little stories of their own.
trivia: Detailed miniature houses called baby houses were popular with wealthy adults in 1600s Europe.
artBrief: Open-front miniature house with tiny rooms, pink walls, red roof, white trim; front view.

name: Rocking Horse
summary: A carved wooden horse on curved rockers with a yarn mane, ready for endless gallops going nowhere.
trivia: Rocking horses with bow-shaped rockers became popular in England in the 1700s.
artBrief: Wooden horse on curved rockers, dapple white body, red saddle, brown yarn mane; side view.

name: Hammock
summary: A swinging fabric sling tied up with rope, where a companion can sway gently into a deep nap.
trivia: Hammocks were developed by Indigenous peoples of the Americas and later adopted by sailors.
artBrief: Curved striped hammock slung between two ropes; red, yellow, white stripes, side view.

name: Night Light
summary: A tiny, soft glowing lamp that keeps the bedroom gently lit so no companion fears the dark.
wit: Monsters hate this one weird trick.
trivia: Dim warm light at night disturbs sleep less than bright blue-white light.
artBrief: Small mushroom-shaped lamp glowing soft yellow on dark background; yellow, cream, navy.

name: Coat Rack
summary: A tall wooden stand with pegs at the top for hanging coats, hats and scarves by the door.
wit: A tree that only grows hats.
trivia: Bentwood coat stands were mass produced in the 1800s using steam to bend the wood.
artBrief: Tall coat stand with curved pegs, scarf and hat hanging; brown, red scarf, blue hat.

name: Umbrella Stand
summary: A tall bucket by the front door where wet umbrellas and walking sticks drip dry.
trivia: Umbrella stands became common hallway furniture in Victorian homes.
artBrief: Tall cylinder bucket with two umbrella handles poking out; brown, red, blue handles.

name: Folding Screen
summary: A hinged wooden screen with fabric panels that folds out to divide a room or hide a messy corner.
trivia: Folding screens were invented in China and spread to Japan, where painted screens became an art form.
artBrief: Three-panel zigzag folding screen, cream panels with pink blossom, brown frame; front view.

name: Cradle
summary: A small rocking basket bed with a soft blanket where the youngest companions are lulled to sleep.
trivia: Gentle rocking motion has been shown to help both babies and adults fall asleep faster.
artBrief: Small wicker cradle on curved rockers, blue blanket, tan weave; side view.

name: Blanket Fort
summary: A secret hideout made by draping blankets over chairs, the cosiest headquarters in the whole house.
trivia: Building forts from blankets and furniture is a favourite childhood activity in many countries.
artBrief: Blanket draped over two chairs forming a tent, peeking eyes in dark gap; purple, yellow, brown.

name: Kitchen
summary: The warm room of a house built around a cooking fire, where meals are prepared for everyone.
trivia: The word kitchen comes from the Latin coquina, meaning a place for cooking.
artBrief: A small house cut-away showing a hearth and a pot; warm orange, brown, cream.

name: Bathroom
summary: A small room of the house set aside for washing, bathing and splashing about.
wit: The only room where puddles are allowed.
trivia: For centuries many homes had no bathroom; people washed in a basin or at public baths.
artBrief: Small room cut-away with a wooden tub and bucket; light blue walls, brown wood, white.

name: Wooden Bowl
summary: A round, shallow bowl carved from a single piece of wood, ready to hold food or water.
wit: Half a bucket, twice as useful.
trivia: Wooden bowls were traditionally turned on a lathe from green, freshly cut wood.
artBrief: Single round wooden bowl seen from slight above; warm brown with darker grain rings.

name: Chopping Board
summary: A thick, flat slab of hardwood used to chop vegetables and fruit without scratching the counter.
trivia: Wood boards are naturally gentle on knife edges compared with glass or stone.
artBrief: Rectangular wooden board with a handle hole and a few chopped carrot rounds; tan, orange.

name: Rolling Pin
summary: A smooth wooden cylinder with handles, rolled across dough to flatten it for bread and cookies.
trivia: Some rolling pins are carved with patterns to press designs into cookies.
artBrief: Horizontal wooden rolling pin with two knob handles; light tan, brown outline, flour dusting.

name: Towel
summary: A thick, soft square of absorbent cloth used to dry off after a bath or a splash.
trivia: Looped terry cloth towels became common in the 1800s once weaving machines could make the loops.
artBrief: Folded fluffy towel with striped edge; soft teal, white stripe, grey shadow.

name: Washtub
summary: A wide, low wooden tub made by sawing a barrel in half, used for laundry and baths.
wit: Half a barrel, full of bubbles.
trivia: Sawing an old barrel in half was a classic way to make a washtub or planter.
artBrief: Low round wooden tub with metal hoops and soap suds; brown wood, grey hoops, white suds.

name: Food Bowl
summary: A sturdy wooden bowl filled with tasty food; companions come here to eat and fill their bellies.
wit: Breakfast, lunch and dinner, served in one bowl.
trivia: Many pets prefer wide, shallow bowls so their whiskers do not brush the sides.
artBrief: Wooden bowl heaped with brown kibble and a little bone on top; brown, tan, cream.

name: Water Bowl
summary: A wooden bowl kept full of fresh, cool water so thirsty companions can drink whenever they like.
trivia: Dogs drink by curling their tongue backwards to scoop water up like a ladle.
artBrief: Wooden bowl with bright blue water and a ripple and a droplet above; brown, blue, white.

name: Feeding Trough
summary: A long wooden trough that holds enough food for a whole house of hungry companions at once.
wit: Everyone gets a seat at this table.
trivia: Troughs have been used on farms for thousands of years to feed livestock together.
artBrief: Long low wooden trough on short legs filled with grain; brown, gold, dark outline.

name: Dish Rack
summary: A slatted wooden rack beside the sink where freshly washed bowls and plates stand up to drip dry.
trivia: Plate racks over the sink let dishes drip straight back into the basin as they dry.
artBrief: Small wooden slatted rack holding three upright plates; brown, white plates, blue drips.

name: Dining Chair
summary: A sturdy kitchen chair with a high back, made to pull up to the dining table at mealtimes.
wit: Reserved for whoever gets there first.
trivia: The word chair comes from the Greek kathedra, a seat, also the root of cathedral.
artBrief: Wooden ladder-back chair with a red cushion; brown, red, side 3/4 view.

name: Dining Bench
summary: A long wooden bench beside the dining table that seats several companions shoulder to shoulder.
wit: Scoot over, there is always room.
trivia: Benches were the usual seating at tables long before individual chairs became common.
artBrief: Long plain wooden bench with four legs; warm brown, darker wood grain, side view.

name: Highchair
summary: A tall wooden chair with a tray for the smallest companions, so they can eat at table height.
trivia: Highchairs for children appear in European paintings from at least the 1600s.
artBrief: Tall wooden chair with long legs and a front tray; light brown, pastel yellow tray.

name: Cupboard
summary: A tall wooden cabinet with doors and shelves that keeps plates and snacks tidy and close at hand.
wit: What is behind door number one? Snacks.
trivia: Cupboard originally meant a board or table for displaying cups.
artBrief: Tall wooden cupboard with two small doors and round knobs; brown, mustard knobs.

name: Pantry
summary: A small storage room off the kitchen stacked with jars, sacks and treats for hungry companions.
wit: The door everyone pretends not to watch.
trivia: Pantry comes from the old French paneterie, a place where bread was kept.
artBrief: Open pantry door showing shelves of jars and a sack; brown, cream, red and green jars.

name: Kitchen Counter
summary: A long wooden work surface with drawers underneath, used for chopping and preparing meals.
wit: Prep space for professional snack makers.
trivia: Standard kitchen counters are usually around 90 centimetres high.
artBrief: Wooden counter with two drawers and a chopping board on top; brown, light tan top.

name: Wood Stove
summary: A cast-iron cooking stove fed with wood, warming the kitchen while it cooks hot meals.
trivia: Wood-burning cook stoves spread through homes in the 1800s, replacing open hearth cooking.
artBrief: Squat black stove with small chimney pipe and orange glow in the door; black, orange, grey.

name: Bread Oven
summary: A domed brick oven heated with a wood fire, perfect for baking crusty loaves for everyone.
trivia: Domed bread ovens hold heat in their thick walls long after the fire is raked out.
artBrief: Domed brick oven with an arched mouth and a loaf on a peel; terracotta, gold, black.

name: Icebox
summary: An insulated wooden chest that keeps food cool with a block of ice, the ancestor of the fridge.
trivia: Iceboxes needed a fresh block of ice delivered every few days by the iceman.
artBrief: Tall wooden box with metal latch and a pale blue ice block glimpse; brown, silver, ice blue.

name: Spice Shelf
summary: A small wall shelf lined with little jars of colourful spices and dried herbs.
trivia: Pepper was once so valuable it was used to pay rent and taxes.
artBrief: Small wooden wall shelf with five tiny jars in red, yellow, green; brown shelf.

name: Tea Kettle
summary: A round kettle that whistles when the water boils, making warm drinks that cheer everyone up.
wit: It sings when it is ready.
trivia: Whistling kettles work by forcing steam through a small opening that vibrates like a whistle.
artBrief: Round kettle with spout and a little steam curl; copper orange, black handle, white steam.

name: Cookie Jar
summary: A round jar with a lid, always filled with freshly baked cookies for companions who behave.
wit: Hand in the jar? Paw in the jar.
trivia: Cookie jars became popular kitchen keepsakes in the 1930s.
artBrief: Round cream jar with lid knob and two cookies peeking out; cream, brown, light blue.

name: Bread Box
summary: A wooden box with a roll-top lid that keeps fresh bread soft and ready for snacking.
wit: Best thing since sliced bread, it holds sliced bread.
trivia: Bread boxes keep bread fresh by holding in some moisture while letting it breathe.
artBrief: Wooden box with a curved roll-top lid and a loaf inside; brown, golden loaf.

name: Picnic Basket
summary: A woven basket with a lid, packed with sandwiches and a checked blanket for meals outdoors.
wit: Lunch, but make it an adventure.
trivia: Picnics grew popular in the 1800s as people sought relaxed outdoor meals in parks.
artBrief: Woven wicker basket with two lids and a red checked cloth peeking; tan, red, white.

name: Sink
summary: A basin set into the counter with a tap, where dishes and paws get washed after dinner.
wit: Dishes go in, sparkles come out.
trivia: Before indoor plumbing, sinks were filled and emptied by hand with buckets.
artBrief: Counter with an inset basin and a curved tap with a water drop; grey, brown, blue.

name: Water Barrel
summary: A tall wooden barrel held together with hoops, full of fresh water for drinking and washing.
trivia: Barrel makers are called coopers, and their craft is thousands of years old.
artBrief: Upright wooden barrel with dark hoops and a ladle on top; brown, grey, blue water.

name: Bathtub
summary: A long tub to soak in warm water; a relaxing bath restores a companion's health.
trivia: Clawfoot bathtubs became fashionable in the late 1800s.
artBrief: White clawfoot tub with bubbles spilling over the rim; white, gold feet, pale blue.

name: Soaking Tub
summary: An extra deep wooden tub with a little ladder, deep enough for companions to practise swimming.
trivia: Japanese ofuro tubs are traditionally deep wooden tubs for soaking up to the shoulders.
artBrief: Tall round wooden tub with a ladder on the side and blue water with a ripple; brown, blue.

name: Shower
summary: A barrel of water raised high that sprinkles down through holes for a quick, refreshing rinse.
trivia: Simple gravity showers made from raised buckets are still used when camping.
artBrief: Raised barrel with a sprinkler head and falling blue drops; brown, grey, light blue.

name: Towel Rack
summary: A wooden wall rack with pegs where fluffy towels hang to dry after bath time.
wit: A place for every towel and every towel in its place.
trivia: Heated towel rails were first used in the early 1900s, warmed by hot water pipes.
artBrief: Wooden wall rack with two pegs holding a teal towel; brown, teal, white.

name: Bath Mat
summary: A soft, thick mat on the bathroom floor that catches drips from wet feet and paws.
trivia: Bath mats help prevent slips by absorbing water on smooth floors.
artBrief: Rectangular fluffy mat with fringe edges; soft pink, white, viewed from above.

name: Laundry Basket
summary: A big woven basket for carrying dirty clothes to the washtub and clean ones back again.
wit: Half full or half empty, it is always laundry day.
trivia: Before washing machines, laundry day often took a whole day each week.
artBrief: Tall woven basket with a sock and shirt sticking out; tan, blue, white.

name: Wash Basin
summary: A wide bowl of water on a small stand for washing faces, paws and whiskers.
trivia: Wash basins with jugs were a standard bedroom fixture before running water.
artBrief: Small wooden stand holding a round basin and a jug; brown, white, light blue water.

name: Bath Duck
summary: A little carved wooden duck that bobs on the bath water, making bath time playful.
trivia: Toy ducks made of rubber became popular in the 1940s, but carved floating toys are much older.
artBrief: Small yellow duck with orange beak floating on a blue ripple; yellow, orange, blue.

name: Treadmill
summary: A hand-cranked walking belt made from a looped rug, so companions can jog in place for hours.
wit: Miles of running, zero metres travelled.
trivia: Early treadmills in the 1800s were powered by people or animals walking to turn mills.
artBrief: Side view of a wooden-framed treadmill with a striped belt and crank; brown, red, cream.

name: Running Wheel
summary: A big upright wooden wheel with a plank track inside that spins as a companion runs within it.
wit: Round and round, faster and faster.
trivia: Hamsters can run several kilometres a night on an exercise wheel.
artBrief: Large wooden wheel on a stand with plank rungs inside; tan, brown, dark outline.

name: Hurdles
summary: A row of low wooden hurdles that companions sprint toward and leap over to build running speed.
wit: Jump the fence, skip the gate.
trivia: Hurdle races have been part of the modern Olympics since the first Games in 1896.
artBrief: Three small white-and-red striped hurdles in a row, green ground strip; red, white, green.

name: Paddling Pool
summary: A wide, shallow wooden tub filled with water where small companions learn to paddle and float.
wit: A bucket that hit its growth spurt.
trivia: Paddling pools are kept shallow so young swimmers can always touch the bottom.
artBrief: Round wooden tub with blue water and a small ripple; brown staves, light blue, white highlights.

name: Splash Tub
summary: A deep varnished tub that keeps water in, perfect for dunking, splashing and practising strokes.
trivia: Varnish seals wood so water cannot soak in and swell the planks.
artBrief: Glossy dark-brown barrel tub brimming with blue water and splash drops; brown, blue, white.

name: Water Slide
summary: A slippery slide that ends in a splashy pool, training swimming with every exciting landing.
trivia: The first water slides in the early 1900s were simple wooden chutes into lakes.
artBrief: Curved blue slide descending into a round pool with splash; blue, yellow, light blue.

name: Swim Ring
summary: A puffy ring-shaped float that helps nervous companions stay up while they kick and learn to swim.
wit: Floats like a donut, never gets eaten.
trivia: Swim rings are one of the oldest flotation aids, once made from cork or inflated animal skins.
artBrief: Red-and-white striped ring float on blue water, top view; red, white, blue.

name: Punching Bag
summary: A heavy canvas bag stuffed with sawdust and hung from a hook, ready to be thumped for strength.
trivia: Early punching bags were often filled with sand, grain or sawdust.
artBrief: Hanging red cylinder bag on a chain, small dent mark; red, grey chain, dark outline.

name: Wooden Dumbbells
summary: A pair of chunky dumbbells carved from wooden bars and discs for companions to lift and grow stronger.
trivia: Ancient Greek athletes trained with stone or metal hand weights called halteres.
artBrief: Two wooden dumbbells crossed, round discs on short bars; tan, brown, dark outline.

name: Tug Rope
summary: A thick knotted rope for friendly tug-of-war matches between companions, training pulling power.
trivia: Tug of war was an Olympic event from 1900 to 1920.
artBrief: Thick braided rope with knots at both ends, stretched horizontally; beige, brown, red ribbon.

name: Log Lift
summary: A sturdy log fitted with grips that strong companions heave above their heads to build raw power.
trivia: Log lifting is a classic strongman event, adapted from lumberjack contests.
artBrief: Horizontal log with two cut-in handles on a small rack; brown, tan, grey.

name: Trampoline
summary: A springy mat laced tight with rope on a frame, bouncing companions high to train their flying.
wit: The floor that throws you back up.
trivia: The modern trampoline was built in 1936 by gymnast George Nissen.
artBrief: Round black mat with blue padded rim and short legs; black, blue, grey.

name: Rope Swing
summary: A plank seat hung on two ropes that swings companions high into the air to get used to flying.
trivia: Rope swings tied to trees are among the oldest playground toys in the world.
artBrief: Plank seat on two long ropes from a top beam, mid-swing; brown, beige, sky blue.

name: Glider Perch
summary: A tall ladder perch with a cloth wing banner where companions climb up and practise gliding down.
wit: Climb up, spread out, float down.
trivia: Otto Lilienthal made over 2,000 glider flights in the 1890s by jumping from hills.
artBrief: Tall wooden perch with ladder and small fabric wing on top; brown, white, sky blue.

name: Kite Stand
summary: A post with a colourful patchwork kite on a line, teaching companions to catch and ride the wind.
trivia: Kites were flown in China more than 2,000 years ago.
artBrief: Diamond patchwork kite with tail tied to a short post; red, yellow, blue patches.

name: Climbing Wall
summary: A tall board wall dotted with chunky wooden pegs as handholds for long, tiring climbing sessions.
trivia: The first purpose-built artificial climbing wall was made in England in 1964.
artBrief: Upright plank wall with colourful round holds; tan, red, yellow, blue.

name: Jump Rope
summary: A light skipping rope with wooden handles that companions jump over again and again to build stamina.
trivia: Boxers use jump rope to improve footwork and endurance.
artBrief: Looped skipping rope with two wooden handles, arc shape; red rope, tan handles.

name: Balance Beam
summary: A long narrow beam raised over a soft mat, where companions carefully walk to build steady endurance.
wit: One foot, then the other, then panic.
trivia: The Olympic balance beam is only 10 centimetres wide.
artBrief: Long tan beam on two legs above a blue mat, side view; tan, blue, brown.

name: Monkey Bars
summary: A sideways ladder raised on posts that companions cross hand over hand until their arms are tired.
trivia: Monkey bars were invented in the 1920s by lawyer Sebastian Hinton.
artBrief: Horizontal ladder on two A-frame posts, side view; red bars, brown posts.

name: Yoga Mat
summary: A soft padded mat for slow stretches and deep breathing that keeps companions healthy and strong.
trivia: Yoga originated in ancient India and has been practised for over two thousand years.
artBrief: Purple padded mat partly rolled at one end, top 3/4 view; purple, lilac, dark outline.

name: Nap Mat
summary: A cosy folded blanket laid on a rug where tired companions take restorative naps to recover health.
trivia: Short naps of 10 to 20 minutes can improve alertness and mood.
artBrief: Folded green blanket on beige mat with small Z letters; green, beige, white.

name: Massage Roller
summary: A rolling wooden massager with little bumps that soothes sore muscles and keeps companions healthy.
trivia: Wooden massage rollers have been used in traditional therapies in many cultures.
artBrief: Wooden roller with bumpy wheels and a short handle; light tan, brown, dark outline.

name: Ball Pit
summary: A pool filled with soft yarn balls that companions dive and roll in for pure happy play.
wit: Lost a companion? Check the bottom.
trivia: Ball pits became popular in play centres in the 1970s and 80s.
artBrief: Round pit full of colourful balls, one head peeking; red, yellow, blue, green.

name: Sandbox
summary: A low wooden box of soft fine filling for digging, building and burying favourite treasures.
trivia: Sandboxes for children were popularised in Germany in the 1850s as 'sand gardens'.
artBrief: Square wooden box with beige filling and a small toy spade; brown, beige, red.

name: Playground Slide
summary: A ladder up to a smooth varnished chute that companions slide down giggling, again and again.
trivia: The first playground slide is often credited to Charles Wicksteed in England in 1922.
artBrief: Ladder with yellow slide curving down, side view; yellow, red, brown.

name: Seesaw
summary: A long plank balanced on a box so two companions can bounce up and down taking turns.
wit: What goes up must come down. Then up.
trivia: A seesaw is a simple lever balanced on a pivot point called a fulcrum.
artBrief: Long plank tilted on a central box, seats at ends; orange, brown, red.

name: Scratching Post
summary: A wooden post wrapped tight in rope that companions scratch and climb to stay calm and happy.
wit: Save the sofa, use the post.
trivia: Cats scratch to keep claws healthy and to leave scent marks.
artBrief: Vertical post wrapped in beige rope on square base, small top pad; beige, brown, red.

name: Spinning Top
summary: A painted wooden top that whirls on its tip, making curious companions wonder how things work.
trivia: Spinning tops are among the oldest toys, found at ancient archaeological sites.
artBrief: Striped wooden top spinning on its point with motion lines; red, yellow, tan.

name: Building Blocks
summary: A stack of painted wooden blocks that companions build into towers, sparking new ideas and discoveries.
trivia: Friedrich Froebel, founder of kindergarten, designed wooden block sets in the 1800s.
artBrief: Small tower of colourful cube blocks with letters; red, blue, yellow, green.

name: Puzzle Board
summary: A picture board cut into interlocking pieces that companions fit together, sharpening their minds.
trivia: The first jigsaw puzzles were maps cut into pieces to teach geography in the 1760s.
artBrief: Square board with jigsaw pieces, one piece lifted out; blue, green, yellow.

name: Garden Bench
summary: A slatted wooden bench for the garden where companions sit and watch the clouds roll by.
trivia: Public park benches became common in the 1800s as city parks opened.
artBrief: Slatted wooden bench with curved armrests, front view; brown, tan, green grass strip.

name: Flower Box
summary: A long window box planted with bright flowers that brightens up any wall or garden corner.
trivia: Window boxes were popular in ancient Rome for growing herbs and flowers in cities.
artBrief: Wooden box under a window frame with pink and yellow flowers; brown, pink, yellow, green.

name: Bird Bath
summary: A shallow water basin on a pedestal where little birds come to drink and splash in the garden.
trivia: Birds bathe to keep their feathers clean and in good flying shape.
artBrief: Shallow bowl of water on a pedestal with a small bird on rim; grey, light blue, brown.

name: Garden Lantern
summary: A lantern on a fence post that glows softly at night, lighting the garden paths for companions.
wit: Night light for the great outdoors.
trivia: Stone garden lanterns have lit Japanese temple gardens for over a thousand years.
